name: Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Radiographic evidence of vertebral abnormalities including platyspondyly and irregular vertebral endplates
Metaphyseal irregularities and cupping of long bones on radiographs
Presence of short stature and skeletal deformities such as genu valgum or limb bowing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both major radiographic criteria (spinal abnormalities and metaphyseal changes) with supportive clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always definitive due to heterogeneity

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic flattening of vertebral bodies seen on imaging

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metaphyseal cupping and irregularity of long bones

common.notes: Due to skeletal deformities affecting mobility

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits secondary to spinal cord compression
Ophthalmological abnormalities such as refractive errors

laboratory: Generally normal metabolic and hematologic labs
Genetic testing may reveal mutations in genes such as COL2A1 or TRPV4
imaging: Radiographs showing platyspondyly and irregular vertebral endplates
Metaphyseal cupping and irregularities in long bones
genetic: Mutations in COL2A1 gene associated with some forms
Mutations in TRPV4 gene reported in certain subtypes
other: Clinical evaluation of growth parameters and skeletal deformities
Family history may be informative in inherited cases

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent metaphyseal abnormalities without significant spinal involvement
Different genetic mutations (e.g., MCDS associated with COL10A1 mutations)
Distinct genetic mutations (COL2A1 gene mutations more common)

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage deformities
Rapidly worsening skeletal deformities impacting mobility
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Spondylometaphyseal dysplasias. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
